beats.text: In Part 7, the model wrote a note for every flagged image. Here is a real **note**.
A typed model reads it, and answers two questions: was this **escalated**, and is anything **uncertain**?
It said **ninety-seven** percent, and **ninety-three** percent. Both match the record, and it took twenty milliseconds.
Across all **520** real notes, it matched the record on **448**.
I audited the other **72**. In **70** of them, the typed model was the one that was wrong.
**Sixty-five** times it called a fine note uncertain, even though the note says confident defect.
The last **two** were arguable. And **none** of the seventy-two was a real flaw in a note.
A guard that finds no real problem is not worth running. When the writer is almost always right, a checker that is **eighty-six** percent right mostly flags good notes.
